worked_example.problem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of {p} cm. Find the length of a side and the size of an angle.
steps: The three sides are equal: {p} ÷ {3} = {s} cm.

cards.idea: Equilateral: three equal sides; isosceles: two; scalene: none.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is {60}°.
The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
example: Base angles {b}° and {b}°, so the top angle is {180 - 2 * b}°.

check.prompt: In an isosceles triangle each base angle is {b}°. Find the third angle.

misconceptions.explain: There are two base angles of {b}°: take both away.

solution: The two base angles are equal: {b} + {b} = {2 * b}°.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides of {a} cm, {b} cm and {c} cm. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.correct: {a == b && b == c ? 'equilateral' : a == b || b == c || a == c ? 'isosceles' : 'scalene'}

misconceptions.explain: Count the equal sides: three → equilateral, two → isosceles, none → scalene. Here: {a}, {b}, {c}.

questions.prompt: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of {p} cm. How long is each side?

misconceptions.explain: There are three equal sides: divide by {3}.

questions.prompt: In an isosceles triangle each base angle is {b}°. Find the third angle.

misconceptions.explain: There are two base angles of {b}°: take both away.

solution: The two base angles are equal: {b} + {b} = {2 * b}°.

right.text: An equilateral triangle has three angles of 60°.
The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle.
An isosceles triangle has two equal angles.
A triangle can be both right-angled and isosceles.

wrong.text: A scalene triangle has two equal sides.
wrong.explain: A scalene triangle has no equal sides.

wrong.text: An equilateral triangle can have a right angle.
The hypotenuse is next to the right angle.
wrong.explain: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle.
